name: Primal VAE (Ostris, 2x1 / 2x2)
summary: Small (~80M params) image autoencoder that only downsamples 2x into 1 or 2 channels; with a 4x4 patch in the DiT it matches the Flux.1 (16 ch @ 8x) or Flux.2 (32 ch @ 8x) latent shape. Latent is trained to be unit-normal, so no scaling/shift factors. Author reports it beats the FLUX.2 VAE on reconstruction. Loads in diffusers and from ai-toolkit checkpoints.

access.notes: Not gated. Needs trust_remote_code=True in diffusers (custom modeling_primal_vae.py). Image sides must be multiples of 16. Experimental release.

procedure: Open huggingface.co/ostris/primal_vae and read the README.
pip install diffusers torch, then AutoModel.from_pretrained('ostris/primal_vae', variant='2x1' or '2x2', trust_remote_code=True).
Use vae.patchify(vae.encode(x), compression=8) to get a Flux.1/Flux.2-shaped latent; decode with vae.decode(vae.unpatchify(tokens)).

verdict.why: Primary HF repo, Apache-2.0 LICENSE file, not gated, real weights; useful building block for people training diffusion models. Reconstruction claim is the author's own and early.

image.alt: Sample image (red-haired woman playing chess in a park) from Ostris's overnight MOSS Image run trained on the Primal VAE 2x1 latent
